scope.description: Opt-in sealed preservation of independently admitted private metadata at unchanged typed fields and unchanged raw lines, with existing credential and installed-hook boundaries retained.
excluded: Approval or installation of any actual new preservation seed; that has a separate private digest-bound review.
Changing the fixed baseline, existing artifact admissions, scanner policy, remote policy or Git configuration.
Operating-system-account isolation or protection from an administrator replacing the trusted runtime.

criteria.evidence: Baseline/seed Git and raw-byte bindings, same-mode existing predecessor, exact private-field inventory and stable key/record-ID selectors are required. Duplicate keys/IDs, indexed private selectors, private aliases, cycles, merge keys, unsupported tags, decoded private mapping keys, multiline private values and new or moved fields fail closed.

Each admitted private field preserves the exact complete raw line, not merely a decoded value. Baseline, seed, predecessor and successor selectors and line digests must agree; harmless public line shifts can pass but value, encoding and line-ending changes cannot.

The isolated worker executes its authenticated held source. The parser imports only the exact authenticated pure-Python archive held in memory. Substituted workers and parsers are denied; mutable live repository modules cannot replace the sealed worker/parser sources.

Only admitted unchanged metadata lines are removed from the private-path/email text check. The full original unmasked raw payload still reaches pinned gitleaks; preservation is not a new credential exception. Exact historical artifact admissions retain their own existing byte-bound authority.

The same-mode predecessor and seed ancestry are checked; deletion/reintroduction and merge edges cannot silently receive future authority. Installed hook/pre-push fixtures reject parser tampering, new disclosure and commit-hook bypass on push. Protected inventory is rejected before protected blob reads.

checks.selection: All 11 methods containing preservation in tests/security/test_prospective_privacy.py, plus test_installed_retention_receipt_allows_commit_push_and_denies_new_disclosure, test_reviewed_binary_passes_real_commit_push_and_changed_image_is_denied, and test_protected_index_rejected_before_blob_reads.
checks.provenance: Actual synthetic Git/hook replay at fixed predecessor HEAD; producer reported exact before/after hashes matching this scope and unchanged HEAD. The reviewer inspected these tests and their changed implementation, then rebound the same bytes to the candidate.

coverage: Unchanged typed field/raw line across harmless line shift
checks.provenance: Fresh -I -S -B subprocess executed authenticated held worker and sealed parser bytes with synthetic values only; exit 0 and empty stderr. No Git mutation, real seed or ordinary data used.
All three raw source hashes equal the frozen review hashes and each explicitly named git --no-replace-objects candidate blob. Performed in the 21-path combined component binding check.
Root reported a fresh selected 14-method privacy run at the fixed candidate with production inputs frozen and no Git changes. Not represented as an independently rerun full module.

notes: Earlier forged-worker and lookalike-tag tests-first failures remain adverse development history; the current exact source and replay include their closures. This review does not rewrite those results.
The fixed baseline, actual prior 130-entry registry and proposed 98-field seed were not read during the initial code review. Approval of the new preservation digest is explicitly separate.
No whole privacy test module or broader repository audit was redundantly replayed by this reviewer; selected real boundaries and incremental independent probes address the changed risk surface.
limitations: This disposition approves only the bounded implementation at this candidate, not an arbitrary registry or future metadata disclosure.
No protected witness content, sibling workspace, ordinary project/vault/policy runtime or remote repository was accessed by this reviewer.
No hooks were installed and no Git configuration or refs were changed by this review.
